project: Personal video tool for the English AI-avatar YouTube channel 'Mamaw Birdie's Mountain Ways'
language_of_videos: English (en-US). Everything the viewer sees or hears is in English.
language_of_user: French. Talk to the user in French.
goal: A personal tool that turns one video idea from the lists below into a finished long-form YouTube video for this AI-avatar channel: the script, the voice, lip-synced avatar clips, B-roll (AI-generated and free stock), verse/text cards, subtitles, the final edit and the publishing pack.

video_method.source: Jake Trinder, 'How to Become Disgustingly Good at YouTube' (youtu.be/Dx-c19qXdxM), Oct 14 2026
video_method.principle: A video is a series system: topic, packaging (title + thumbnail), hook, body and edit must all be right; one wrong decision can sink the video.
topic: Pick topics from what the audience already chooses to watch (revealed preference), not from what we think they need.
For each topic note the floor (median views of a decent video) and the ceiling (best videos) over the last 3–6 months, 8+ min videos.
Check views look real (≈1–5 % likes per view, on-topic comments) and that demand is still active (recent videos still getting views).
Raise the ceiling by attaching the topic to a bigger demand: season, event, culture (Amish, Japanese), well-known store (Walmart, Costco, Aldi).
title: Use a title framing that wins in at least 2–3 different channels or niches, not a single outlier.
Understand why the framing works and only reuse it if that reason is true for our audience (avoid overfitting).
The title must make a promise the video fully delivers; never use false words.
thumbnail: Job 1: stand out in the feed. Job 2: be understood at a glance.
Avatar face + one object/icon that targets the audience + a tension that opens a question; the title closes only part of it.
video_method.edit: The edit matches the promise: calm and warm for our characters, useful B-roll, on-screen text for numbers, no gratuitous effects.

hook_4P.promise: Confirm in one sentence that this is what they clicked for.
hook_4P.proof: Why listen: honest proof only (sources, the character's story told as a story, a shown result). Never fake credentials or numbers.
hook_4P.plan: Announce the steps / number of items and what comes at the end.
hook_4P.persona: Name the viewer: 'if you're over 60', 'if you lost your spouse', 'wenn du einen Diesel fährst'.
hook_4P.timing: All 4 P inside the first 30–45 seconds.

body_acceptance_criteria: Decompose the title's promise: what must be true at the end for the title to be true? Break each answer down again.
That list is the outline; the script is finished only when every condition is met.
Deliver real value fast, then exceed the expectation (one bonus item, a safety tip, a worked example).
Goal is viewer satisfaction, not retention tricks.
after_publish: Early signals: positive comments per view (and what they say), likes per view, subs per view, view curve vs channel average.
A metric tells where to look, not what to change (low CTR → look at the thumbnail and ask why).
Sharp retention drop → inspect that moment (early CTA, a slow part) and cut it.
Write down one lesson per video for the next one.
pre_production_checklist: Topic has a good floor (median) and a high ceiling on videos from the last 3–6 months.
Reference views look real and demand is still active.
Topic is attached to a bigger demand when possible (season, store, culture, event).
Title framing wins in at least 2 different channels and we know why it works for our audience.
Title promise is deliverable and true, no false words.
Thumbnail: avatar face, one audience-targeting object, an open question; understood in 1 second.
Hook has the 4 P (promise, honest proof, plan, persona) in the first 45 seconds.
Script outline = the list of conditions that make the title true; every one is met.
Over-deliver: a bonus, a safety tip, a worked example.
Edit matches the promise: calm, warm, no gratuitous effects.
After 48 h and 7 days: read comments, likes/view, subs/view, retention curve; note one lesson.

title_rule: Clone, word for word, the title of a video that got many views and change only the niche words. If a word would be false for our video ('BANNED', '100% Effective', 'NEVER EXPIRE', an inflated number, 'Industry Buried'), replace only that word. The new ideas below already follow this rule and the video_method.
avatar_rules: Each lip-synced avatar clip is at most 15 seconds; longer passages are split and alternated with B-roll.
Every avatar image comes from the same reference image (same face, clothes, set) — generate the reference first, then use it for every variant.
Faces must stay clearly visible (three-quarter angle at most) or lip-sync fails.
Cover any glitchy lip-sync moment with B-roll while the voice continues.
The avatar is on screen about 20 % of the time (intro, transitions, ending); the rest is B-roll.

segments.part: Hook | Welcome | Item 1 … | Prayer | Blessing | Ending
segments.speaker: BIRDIE | VIRGIL
segments.shot: one of the channel shot_library keys, or BROLL_STOCK / BROLL_AI / TEXT_CARD / VERSE_CARD

production_pipeline: 1. Pick the next video (publishing_order, then new_ideas_oct2026 by priority) or the one the user names.
2. Research: open the reference video(s), read the transcript, note structure and promise; check floor/ceiling and that demand is still active (video_method.topic).
3. Write acceptance criteria from the title (video_method.body_acceptance_criteria), then the script with the 4P hook in the first 45 s.
4. Fact-check every claim: CDC, USDA, NCHFP, NIA, ENERGY STAR, FEMA for every safety, food or money claim. Remove anything unsourced.
5. Check the word count against the channel target.
6. Voice: generate audio per segment with the fixed voice of the speaker.
7. Avatar clips: lip-sync each avatar segment on the right reference image (≤15 s).
8. B-roll: stock first for generic real scenes, AI for specific scenes and for anything showing our characters' places.
9. Edit: voice track, avatar clips, B-roll, text/verse cards, music, subtitles, AI label in the first seconds.
10. QA with video_method.pre_production_checklist and the channel guardrails, export.
11. Publishing pack: title, description (template), chapters, tags, pinned comment, thumbnail; tick 'Altered or synthetic content' in YouTube Studio.
12. After 48 h and 7 days: read the signals listed in video_method.after_publish and write one lesson for the next video.
compliance: AI characters are declared in the channel description and with YouTube's 'altered or synthetic content' setting on every upload.
The characters' memories are presented as stories; they never claim to be real people or give fake credentials.
Affiliate links and the channels' own products are clearly labelled (FTC).
No medical, legal or financial promises.

channel.about:
Welcome to Mamaw Birdie's Mountain Ways.

Up in the Blue Ridge, folks never had much money — so they learned to make do. How to keep a house cool without air conditioning and warm without a big gas bill. How to clean without a cupboard full of store-bought bottles. How to keep a family fed through a long mountain winter. Those old ways saved families a lot of money, and most of them still work today.
On this channel, Mamaw Birdie and Papaw Virgil share those ways — the thrift, the know-how and the stories behind them — so you can spend a little less and live a little simpler.
New videos every Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.
📖 Mamaw Birdie’s Mountain Thrift Book: [your link]
Mamaw Birdie and Papaw Virgil are AI-presented storytellers. The ways shared here come from Appalachian tradition and are checked against reliable sources. Always use common sense, and follow the safety instructions on any product you use.

BIRDIE.name: Bernice 'Birdie' Hollins
BIRDIE.bio: Youngest of seven children, grew up on a small farm in the Blue Ridge Mountains of southwest Virginia. Nicknamed 'Birdie' because she always sang while hanging laundry. Kept house all her life: Monday wash day, a pantry that lasts all winter, a budget where nothing is wasted. Married to Virgil for 58 years, three children, nine grandchildren.
BIRDIE.topics: Cooking and pantry, cleaning and homemade products, sewing and mending, folklore and memories.
BIRDIE.tone: Warm, a little teasing; always tells a story before giving the tip.
BIRDIE.voice: Woman around 78, soft Appalachian accent, slow pace, warm.

VIRGIL.name: Virgil Hollins
VIRGIL.bio: Worked forty years at the county sawmill and always fixed everything himself. Never threw a tool away and knows the name of every tree on the hill. In his workshop, everything has its place and everything gets fixed.
VIRGIL.topics: Tools and maintenance, heating and wood, pests, garden, fences, making do.
VIRGIL.line: If it ain't broke, oil it.
VIRGIL.tone: Calm, few words, dry humor. Teases Birdie, who always has the last word.
VIRGIL.voice: Man around 80, deep and steady voice, a little dry humor.
VIRGIL.use: Optional second voice: tool/heating/pest topics and short exchanges with Birdie.

opening_exchange: BIRDIE: Well, hey there, honey. Come on up on the porch and sit a spell. I'm Mamaw Birdie…
VIRGIL: …and I'm the one who fixes whatever she breaks.

character_rule: They are fictional storytellers declared as AI characters. Their memories are stories that introduce real, checked know-how; they never claim to be real people or that their memories are real facts.

format.structure: A numbered list (10–30 items) with family memories between items; avatar ≈ 20 % of the screen time (intro, transitions, ending), the rest period-style and how-to B-roll.
format.script_length: ≈ 3,600–3,800 words for 20 min, ≈ 4,800–4,950 words for 30 min (always under 5,000).
parts: 4P hook in Birdie's voice (promise, honest proof = her life story, plan, persona).
The numbered items: memory → the old way → why it works → today's safe version and cost.
Safety reminder, the 'Mamaw's rule' summary, call to comment, the book if the link exists, warm goodbye.

BIRDIE_PORCH.prompt: A 78-year-old Appalachian grandmother sitting in a worn wooden rocking chair on the front porch of an old log cabin in the Blue Ridge Mountains, late afternoon. She has silver hair pinned up in a loose bun, kind deep-set eyes, a lined, weathered face with gentle smile lines. She wears a faded blue cotton print dress with a hand-knit cream cardigan and a simple apron. A wooden bowl of green beans rests on her lap. Behind her, slightly out of focus: rough-hewn log walls, a hanging oil lantern, a quilt draped over the railing, misty green mountain ridges. Soft natural golden-hour light. Eye level, medium shot, 50mm lens, f/2.8, shallow depth of field, realistic skin texture with natural wrinkles and age spots, documentary photography style, 16:9.

safety_facts: Indoor heat: keep at least 68 °F (NIA, hypothermia risk for seniors).
Never use an oven, grill or generator indoors to heat (carbon monoxide); CO detector.
Space heater: 3 feet clearance, plugged straight into the wall.
Average heating saving with a programmable thermostat ≈ 15 % (ENERGY STAR) — never invent big savings.
Rodent cleanup: bleach 1:10, gloves, don't sweep droppings (CDC).
Never mix bleach with vinegar or ammonia.
Food storage and canning: USDA / NCHFP rules only.
